extracted.intended_audience: ALSC award committee chairs and members (Caldecott Medal Committee and other ALSC award committees)
extracted.subtask_description: Operational and evaluative guidelines for ALSC award committees (particularly the Randolph Caldecott Medal Committee) covering book discussion etiquette, balloting rules, confidentiality, publicity, roles/responsibilities, eligibility/checklist, and social-media/publication restrictions for committee members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refer to official criteria during discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer back to the criteria to keep the discussion focused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the award’s stated criteria as the touchstone for discussion so conversation remains relevant to eligibility and merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness in discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Be concise—be sure that what you have to say adds to the discussion; try not to repeat what others have said.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid repetition; each contribution should add distinct value to the committee’s evaluation of a book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speak to the group and listen openly
rubrics_metrics.description: Speak to the group as a whole. Listen openly to other committee members and respond thoughtfully to what they have to say.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address the committee collectively rather than individuals; practice active listening and respectful, thoughtful responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid personal anecdotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Be courteous and refrain from relating personal anecdotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep discussion professional and focused on the book’s merits rather than personal stories that do not illuminate evaluation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison restricted to eligible books
rubrics_metrics.description: Make comparisons but only in relationship to other eligible books. That is, do not compare a book with an author’s body of work or with books published before the year under consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons must be limited to contemporaneous eligible titles to ensure fairness and adherence to the award year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start with strengths before weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus first on a book’s strengths before its weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin discussion by articulating what the book does well to provide balanced evaluation and context for any criticisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be even-handed in length of discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Be as even-handed as possible. Books do not always require the same length of discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for fairness in attention given; however, allocate discussion time proportionate to the book’s significance and committee interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closing statement by introducer
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclude with a closing statement from the committee member who introduced the book under discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice provides balance by allowing the introducer to summarize and respond to both negative and positive points raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ballot ranking format
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members list first, second, and third place votes for the award in an online tool created by the Awards Coordinator and sent to the Chair for distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the prescribed online balloting tool and rank up to three titles per ballot as instructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point assignment for ballots
rubrics_metrics.description: In tabulating ballot results, the online tool will assign four points to each first-place vote, three points to each second-place vote, and two points to each third-place vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring is weighted by rank: 1st=4 pts, 2nd=3 pts, 3rd=2 pts; the online tool handles tabulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Winning threshold and margin
rubrics_metrics.description: A book must receive at least eight first-choice votes at four points each for a total of at least thirty-two points, and it must have an eight-point lead over the book receiving the next highest number of points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both the absolute point minimum (32) and the relative lead (8 points) are required for a winner to be declared under the standard formula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chair voting recommendation when one member down
rubrics_metrics.description: If the committee is operating an odd number of members down, it is recommended that the Chair refrain from voting, as an even number of committee members makes it significantly harder for a book to achieve the margin of points needed to win.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair should consider abstaining from voting when the committee has an odd number of absences to maintain reasonable chance for a decisive outcome; Awards Coordinator can adjust formula if an even number down.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjusting balloting formula for absences
rubrics_metrics.description: If a committee is operating an even number of members down, the Awards Coordinator can adjust the formula used in the online balloting tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Awards Coordinator has discretion to modify the balloting calculation to account for multiple absences; follow any adjusted instructions provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor book consideration after winner selected
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is a winner, the committee next considers whether to select Honor books, and if so, what procedure should be used to make this selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Honor book selection is a separate decision after choosing the winner; the committee determines the method (e.g., reuse selection ballot or conduct an additional ballot).

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-balloting requires further discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee may not proceed to another ballot without a second round of book discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each new ballot must be preceded by further discussion to allow reconsideration of titles before re-voting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdraw zero-vote books after first ballot
rubrics_metrics.description: By consensus the committee may choose to withdraw from the discussion list all books that received no votes on the first ballot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawing zero-vote books is optional and requires consensus; withdrawn books are permanently eliminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdraw minimally supported books by consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: By consensus the committee may choose to withdraw additional books that received minimal support on the first ballot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee may remove low-support titles to narrow the field before re-balloting; withdrawn titles cannot be reconsidered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent elimination upon withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: Once withdrawn from the discussion list, a book is permanently eliminated from consideration for the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal is final—books removed after discussion cannot re-enter the current year’s consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeat discussion and balloting until winner
rubrics_metrics.description: If the first ballot does not produce a winner, the committee follows the procedures outlined for re-balloting, alternating between discussion and re-balloting until a winner is selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continue cycles of focused discussion followed by ballots as necessary; no shortcutting the requirement for discussion before subsequent ballots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor books naming parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no requirement that Honor Books be named and no rule dictating the number of Honor Books to be named; there is an expectation that Honor Books be truly distinguished, not merely strong contenders for the Award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Honor Books should be reserved for clearly distinguished titles; committee discretion governs whether and how many are named.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor book ballot options
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether to use the winning selection ballot to choose Honor Books (looking at titles with next highest points) or to ballot one more time is a committee decision; only one additional Honor Book ballot is allowed and consists of titles from the winning selection ballot that received points (winner eliminated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee may select Honors from existing tallies or conduct one extra ballot limited to previously-scoring titles; consensus may withdraw titles with no remaining support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor books announced alphabetically
rubrics_metrics.description: Honor Books are announced to the public in alphabetical order by title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public announcement order is alphabetical; do not imply ranking among Honor Books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality: do not disclose others’ reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not disclose reasons (other than your own) given by individual committee members for nominating, supporting, or removing a book from consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the Chair or a designate will present the committee’s collective reasons; individual members must keep their explanations private.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality: do not disclose specific titles under consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific titles or lists of titles under consideration should not be discussed publicly. Remember that all eligible books are under consideration prior to the Midwinter Selection meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Never reveal which books were suggested, nominated, or under active consideration before selection; confidentiality applies at all times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality: do not disclose ballots/vote counts
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of ballots necessary for any decision or the vote in any balloting must not be disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vote counts and ballot tallies are confidential committee business and must not be revealed publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chair drafts press release with justifications
rubrics_metrics.description: After the selection process is complete the Chair prepares a draft press release, usually with assistance from committee members, using background information and justification statements about the winning books as background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair compiles rationale and background for the winner(s) and provides the draft to ALA Communications & Marketing Office (CMO) by the deadline and in the designated format; CMO finalizes it for distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award notification coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee Chair will receive information concerning the timing and method of communication with the award winners from the CMO and the Awards Coordinator prior to LibLearnX and will inform all the committee members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow CMO/Awards Coordinator directions closely for notifying winners and coordinate committee communications accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press conference attendance and punctuality
rubrics_metrics.description: At the ALA YMA Press Conference, committee members are asked to be present and to stand for recognition when their award is announced; committee reconvenes at CMO headquarters and should be present a few minutes before scheduled photo time to avoid delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee must be punctual and present for photos and announcement; the press conference must start on time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public relations guidance for committee members
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members may work with local news media to publicize awards, emphasizing librarians’ role in selection, the value of distinguished books for young readers, the award criteria, and the committee’s reasons as stated in the press release; if contacted by national media, committee members should immediately email details to the Chair, PGC, ALSC Executive Director and current ALSC President and await instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public comments should reflect the official justification and respect confidentiality; coordinate with leadership for national media contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chair correspondence responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chair handles correspondence specific to their committee’s selection and work: sends appreciation letters to members and employers; sends the next Chair a list of any potentially eligible books with next year’s copyright date that the committee identified (with caution about confidentiality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep institutional record-keeping and handover materials while avoiding disclosure of confidential deliberations or full discussion lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final reporting and recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chair submits a final Quarterly Report, along with meeting minutes, to appropriate ALSC leadership and may send recommendations regarding selection policies, practices, and procedures to the new Chair, the PGC, and the Awards Coordinator, with copy to the Executive Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reporting channels to propose improvements; recommendations can range from minor process tweaks to items requiring Board action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation for presentation and contact with winners
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chair works with the ALSC Awards Coordinator to make arrangements for presentation of the award, communicating with winning author(s)/illustrator(s) and publisher(s); the Chair prepares remarks for the Award presentation as directed by the ALSC office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate logistics and communications through ALSC staff; prepare appropriate introductory/acceptance remarks per direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation and release timeline for committee materials
rubrics_metrics.description: ALSC preserves suggestion lists, nomination lists, and justification statements (with names redacted); minutes (redacting confidential points); the Chair’s press remarks; copies of congratulatory letters, and the Chair’s award presentation remarks, adding these materials to the archive and permitting publication after 50 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Archival retention is governed by ALSC policy; materials may be published only after the 50-year embargo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusion of service file transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chair completes their term by sending all committee files to the ALSC Executive Director (including copies of committee communications, letters/emails, and congratulatory letters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure a complete and confidential handover of administrative materials to ALSC at term end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chair role: balance and facilitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chair must maintain a delicate balance between presiding and being a member: limit remarks to points not already made, speak later in discussion, speak only to matters felt strongly about, and be ready to abstain from voting if appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair should set a constructive tone, ensure equitable participation, and avoid dominating the discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chair administrative duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chair attends orientation; places calls for book recommendations; checks eligibility of suggested/nominated books (with PGC help); answers correspondence promptly; submits budget requests; maintains financial records; prepares quarterly reports; contacts non-participating members; represents the committee at leadership meetings; attends press conference briefing; presents problems to PGC and Awards Coordinator as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair is expected to manage both substantive and administrative tasks and to communicate with staff and membership per established timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative assistant appointment and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chair may request an administrative assistant (a volunteer) to help with workload; although not a voting member, the assistant is held to the same confidentiality standards and may participate virtually if requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative assistants can support logistics but must abide by confidentiality and are not required to attend conferences in person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soliciting ALSC membership suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chair is responsible for calling for book recommendations several times during the year in ALSC outlets (blog, website, ALA Connect, tweets, journal); suggestions are collated via an online tool and are accepted up to two weeks before LibLearnX Selection Meeting; only books nominated by committee members are considered at LibLearnX selection meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While member-at-large suggestions should be taken seriously, the formal nomination and LibLearnX consideration process relies on committee nominations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Group Consultant (PGC) role
rubrics_metrics.description: A PGC is assigned to address committee questions regarding procedure, personnel, and eligibility; the PGC reviews procedures annually, makes recommendations, attends introductory/initial meetings to explain their role, and advises on unusual issues, especially those concerning the Chair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the PGC for procedural or eligibility questions and for escalation of unresolved internal issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: ALSC staff responsibilities supporting committee
rubrics_metrics.description: ALSC staff check eligibility of appointees, send formal invitations, provide contact forms and rosters to the Chair, assist calls for membership submissions, create online forms for suggestions/nominations/balloting, secure meeting rooms, provide contact info for winners, work with CMO on announcements, update awards lists, arrange logistics for presentations, and handle engraving and awards preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committees should coordinate administrative needs through the specified ALSC staff contacts and follow provided processes/forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: ALSC President oversight duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The ALSC President appoints committee members and the Chair, makes appointments to fill vacancies, deals with conflicts of interest or non-participation (in consultation), and presides at announcement and presentation ceremonies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive oversight and appointment authority rests with the ALSC President; consult the President/Executive Committee for high-level issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospective member conflict-of-interest checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Prospective members must answer questions about prior service on other ALA units, contracts for children’s trade books during service, recent employment/consulting for publishers/authors/illustrators, close relatives who are authors/illustrators or employed by publishers, ownership of >5% equity in a U.S. trade publisher, personal relationships creating perceived conflicts, ability to attend meetings, access to newly published children's books, and recent service on certain committees; 'yes' answers require contacting the Executive Director before accepting appointment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure is mandatory; failure to disclose may lead to immediate dismissal. Prospective members must verify understanding of service guidelines and social media restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media and publication restrictions during term
rubrics_metrics.description: Members should not use social media or electronic forms of communication in relation to eligible titles during their term of service (July 1 start or immediately upon appointment), excluding closed committee forums; prohibited outlets include Facebook, Twitter, Goodreads, LibraryThing, blogs, and review websites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee members may not blog, tweet, or otherwise publicly discuss any aspect of eligible titles during their term; closed, private committee communications are exempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on signed reviews and permitted alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Award committee members may not publish bylined articles or signed reviews that feature titles eligible for their award during their term; permitted alternatives include unsigned reviews, signed reviews of foreign publications outside eligibility, and other committee-specific exceptions (e.g., Batchelder, Sibert, Geisel allowances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members may write unsigned reviews; specific committee exceptions allow certain signed reviews (details vary by committee). Consult the policy for permitted categories (imports, non-U.S. books, books without illustrations, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: When to cease and resume signed reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: ALSC policy indicates you may not engage in print or electronic communication regarding eligible titles during your term (starts July 1); however, once the committee’s selections have been announced at the LibLearnX Youth Media Awards Press Conference, you may resume writing bylined reviews and blogging even though the term ends at the following Annual Conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The effective blackout period is July 1 through the public announcement; be cautious about galleys and potential eligibility tied to publication date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Galley/publication cutoff safety rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The prohibition includes galleys produced after July 1 because publication dates can be delayed; ALSC uses the July 1 cutoff for books in galley form to ensure consistency and avoid accidental eligibility conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not review or publicly discuss galleys issued after July 1 during your term, as they might become eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on writing teacher/reader guides
rubrics_metrics.description: Members are not permitted to write teachers’ or readers’ group guides for children’s trade-book publishers during their term because this is considered serving in an advisory capacity to a trade publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creating advisory content for trade publishers is disallowed while serving on an award committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library reference assistance not disqualifying
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing ordinary library reference assistance (e.g., helping an author with research) does not count as serving in an advisory capacity and does not disqualify a member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine reference help is acceptable; more formal advisory roles are not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dedication or eligible book authored for member is disqualifying
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is a children’s book being dedicated to a committee member that will come out during the term of service, that is a problem and the member may not accept appointment (or is expected to resign as soon as they find out).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct personal dedications or similar situations that create appearance of interest require resignation or disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Close personal relationships may affect eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Having a friend who is a children’s book author may disqualify service if that friend publishes eligible books during the member’s year; if no eligible book is published during the year, it may not be an issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess potential conflicts on a case-by-case basis and disclose to Executive Director if uncertain.
